ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r1.claim: The preceding sūrahs explain that Quraysh received peace and sustenance because of the House, blessings that should have led them to worship God sincerely and fulfil its purpose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r1.anchor: These blessings should have induced them to worship the Lord of this Sacred House with all sincerity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r2.claim: The paired sūrahs al-Mā‘ūn and al-Kawthar portray Quraysh custodians as failed trustees who deserve removal, with the trust passing to worthy people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r2.anchor: they are no longer fit to be the trustees of this exalted House

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r6.claim: The House was built both as the centre for worship of the one God and to meet the physical and emotional needs of orphans and the poor.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r6.anchor: the centre of worship of the one and only God; and secondly, to cater for the needs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r7.claim: Its custodians were charged with these tasks, but the unworthy leaders cannot fulfil them, so the following sūrah settles their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p469/r7.anchor: since the individuals whose unworthy characters are depicted cannot be expected to fulfil the duty

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r1.claim: The opening question engages the reader by expressing surprise and dislike at a person's or group's attitude.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r1.anchor: is used to engage the attention of a reader by expressing surprise and dislike at the attitude of a person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r2.claim: Al-dīn here means reward and punishment, as in the description of God as Master of the Day of Judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r2.anchor: here means “reward and punishment” as in

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r3.claim: The relative pronoun has no stated antecedent, but context identifies Abū Lahab as its referent.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r3.anchor: the context readily indicates that Ab ū Lahab’s character is being symbolized

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r4.claim: Abū Lahab was extremely rich and stingy and controlled the House's treasury at the time of revelation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r4.anchor: He was an extremely rich yet stingy person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r5.claim: The sūrah Lahab depicts Abū Lahab's mean personality and ultimate destruction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r5.anchor: His mean personality and his ultimate destruction are depicted in a complete sūrah – Lahab

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r6.claim: Abū Lahab treated the treasury as his property and used its funds personally, making him Makkah's Qarūn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r6.anchor: considered the rif ādah as his own property and consumed its funds for personal purposes

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r8.claim: Calling him a denier of reward and punishment identifies his inner self.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p470/r8.anchor: denier of reward and punishment) highlights

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r1.claim: Denial of judgement removes the motive to spend for God or others; such a person spends only for himself or to display false concern, while belief in the Final Day prompts generosity without self-interest.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r1.anchor: A person who denies the Day of Judgement cannot have any motivation to expend his wealth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r2.claim: Sūrah al-Layl likewise contrasts giving and fearing God with greed, heedlessness, and the respective easy and hard paths.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p471/r2.anchor: This fact has also been highlighted in Sūrah al-Layl

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r5.claim: Most commentators call the surah Meccan; Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatada say Madinan, while Hibat Allāh says its halves came down in Mecca and Medina.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r5.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول الجمهور، مدنية في قول ابن عباس وقتادة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r6.claim: Since the previous surah recalled God's favors to Quraysh, this one threatens those who deny resurrection and recompense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r6.anchor: ولما عدد تعالى نعمه على قريش، وكانوا لا يؤمنون بالبعث والجزاء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r7.claim: The passage is attributed to Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, ʿUmar ibn ʿĀʾidh, two hypocrites, or Abū Sufyān, who struck an orphan asking for food after his weekly sacrifice; Ibn Jurayj gives the last report.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p551/r7.anchor: ونزلت في أبي جهل، أو الوليد بن المغيرة، أو العاصي بن وائل، أو عمر بن عائذ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r1.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r1.claim: Al-Ḥawfī takes araʾayta as inform me, with two objects: al-ladhī supplies one and the other is omitted as whether he deserves God's punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r1.anchor: والظاهر أن أرأيت هي التي بمعنى أخبرني، فتتعدى لاثنين، أحدهما الذي، والآخر محذوف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī supplies the omitted second object as asking who the person is; the added address kāf in Ibn ʿAbbās's reading supports inform me, since visual raʾā does not take it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r2.anchor: وقدره الزمخشري: من هو، ويدل على أنها بمعنى أخبرني. قراءة عبد الله أرأيتك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r3.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r3.claim: Al-Ḥawfī also allows literal seeing, with no ellipsis; the question prompts recognition of a person with the described traits.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r3.anchor: قال الحوفي: ويجوز أن تكون من رؤية البصر، فلا يكون في الكلام حذف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r4.claim: Al-dīn means recompense through reward and punishment; al-Zamakhsharī says denial of recompense appears as harshly pushing an orphan away and refusing to urge one's household to feed a poor person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r4.anchor: والدين: الجزاء بالثواب والعقاب. وقال الزمخشري: والمعنى هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses denial as rejecting God's rule; Mujāhid says accounting, while other views say recompense or the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p552/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: بالدين: بحكم الله. وقال مجاهد: بالحساب، وقيل: بالجزاء، وقيل: بالقرآن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers an alternative syntax joining fa-dhālika to the one who denies judgment, omitting the answer to araʾayta, and making the woe to praying hypocrites a description standing for their pronoun; generic singular carries a plural sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r8.anchor: وطريقة أخرى أن يكون فذلك عطفا على الذي يكذب، إما عطف ذات على ذات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.claim: The author calls al-Zamakhsharī's accusative parsing of fa-dhālika strange and unnatural: a nominative subject is immediate, while an accusative would require repeating the verb and pointing needlessly to the person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r9.anchor: فجعل فذلك في موضع نصب عطفا على المفعول، وهو تركيب غريب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r10.claim: The author says a more idiomatic construction would coordinate a following relative clause or use a verb directly, rather than insert the demonstrative in al-Zamakhsharī's proposed parse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p553/r10.anchor: بل الفصيح أكرمت الذي يزورنا فالذي يحسن إلينا، أو أكرمت الذي يزورنا فيحسن إلينا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r1.claim: He rejects the proposed parsing that makes the demonstrative refer to a separate entity: fa-dhālika points back to the one who denies, so they are not two entities.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r1.anchor: فلا يصح، لأن فذلك إشارة إلى الذي يكذب، فليسا بذاتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r2.claim: The alleged omitted answer to arāʾayta is not an answer; it functions as the second object of arāʾayta.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r2.anchor: وأما قوله: ويكون جواب أرأيت محذوفا، فلا يسمى جوابا، بل هو في موضع المفعول الثاني لأرأيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r3.claim: He rejects an interrogative hamza before niʿma, since niʿma and biʾsa are performative expressions and interrogation applies only to declarative statements.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p554/r3.anchor: فهمزة الاستفهام لا نعلم دخولها على نعم ولا بئس، لأنهما إنشاء، والاستفهام لا يدخل إلا على الخبر

FARRA:v3p294#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p294#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v3p294#2/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads araʾaytaka, with an added kāf that may be used or omitted without changing the meaning.
FARRA:v3p294#2/r1.anchor: والكاف صلة تكون ولا تكون ، والمعنى واحد.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r1.claim: The surah is also called al-Din, Ara'ayta, and al-Takdhib; its purpose is to show denial of resurrection and recompense as the root of vile character and contempt for people's rights.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r1.anchor: وتسمى الدين وتسمى أرأيت والتكذيب . مقصودها التنبيه على أن التكذيب بالبعث لأجل الجزاء أبو الخبائث

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r2.claim: Its names clearly point to its theme on reflection: it directly forbids vice and indirectly calls people toward noble conduct.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r3.claim: The basmala praises God's perfection, mercy to both good and bad, and the completion of grace for His close servants through the joy of communion.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#s107/r3.anchor: الذي تعالت عظمته عن كل شائبة نقص فكان له كل كمال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r1.claim: The preceding dealings with Quraysh show that God punishes transgression and treats people with wise gentleness, so He will not leave them without recompense; Quraysh were commanded to thank Him through exclusive worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r1.anchor: فكان معرفا بأن فاعله لا يترك الناس سدى من غير جزاء , وأمرهم آخر قريش بشكر نعمته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r2.claim: Belief in recompense motivates noble character and restrains vice; the author marvels that anyone could deny it despite the clear evidence of divine wisdom, and says the surah depicts the denier repulsively to urge belief.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r2.anchor: وعجب ممن يكذب بالجزاء مع وضوح الدلالة عليه بحمة الحكيم , ووصف المكذب به بأوصاف هم منها في غاية النفرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r3.claim: The direct address 'Have you seen?' is aimed at the Prophet as the community's leader, since he alone fully understands this matter.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r3.anchor: فقال خاصا بالخطاب رأس الأمة إشارة إلى أنه لا يفهم هذا الأمر حق فهمه غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r4.claim: Here 'Have you seen?' means 'tell me'; since it governs two objects, the omitted second object is understood as asking whether the denier deserves punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r4.anchor: ولما كان فعل الرؤية بمعنى أخبرني , المتعدي إلى مفعولين , كان تقدير المفعول الثاني : أليس جديرا بالانتقام منه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.claim: He links this surah to earlier warnings about human ignorance and injustice and cites the ungrateful person, humanity in loss, and the man who thinks wealth makes him immortal.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r5.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تضمنت السور المتقدمة من الوعيد لمن انطوى على ما ذكر فيها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r6.claim: He says those earlier traits also produce obsession with accumulation, slander and mockery, and pride in the people of the Elephant.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541#2/r6.anchor: وانجر أثناء ذلك مما تثيره هذه الصفات الأولية ما ذكر فيها أيضا كالشغل بالتكاثر , والطعن على الناس ولمزهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p544/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p544/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p544/r15.claim: The seven-verse al-Ma'un parallels seven-verse al-Anfal in number and in turning its ending back to its opening; al-Anfal expands the same lesson, so readers should notice the connection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p544/r15.anchor: وكما التقى آخرها بأولها التقت السورة كلها مع مناظرتها في العدد من أول القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r1.claim: The opening question prompts the listener to recall anyone he knows with the described traits.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r1.anchor: هذا توقيف وتنبيه لتتذكر نفس السامع كل من يعرفه بهذه الصفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r2.claim: Abu Amr sometimes hamzates araʾayta; Nafi and the other readers do not.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r2.anchor: وهمز أبو عمرو: «أرأيت» بخلاف عنه ولم يهمزها نافع وغيره،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r3.claim: Din means recompense in reward and punishment, with accounting close to recompense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p527#2/r3.anchor: و «الدين» الجزاء ثوابا وعقابا، والحساب هنا قريب من الجزاء

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، عكرمة، قتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Ikrima, and Qatada classify the seven-verse sura as Meccan.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r1.anchor: قيل: مكية، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، وعكرمة، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.speaker: الضحاك، الواقدي
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Waqidi classify the sura as Medinan.

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.claim: Muqatil says it is Meccan through the mention of the needy, with the remainder Medinan.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r3.anchor: مكية إلى قوله: (المسكين) وباقي السورة مدنية، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.claim: A report transmitted from Ubayy says reciting this sura brings God's forgiveness for one who pays zakat; no grading is given.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r4.anchor: وعن أبي، عن النبي، صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (أرأيت) غفر الله له

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.claim: After recounting favors to Quraysh, the sura marvels at their conduct despite Meccan security and provision, then their denial of the Prophet and his prophethood.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r5.anchor: افتتح هذه السورة تعجبا من حالهم مع عظم النعم عليهم بمكة من الأمن والرزق

JISHUMI:v10p7555/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r10.claim: Al-din can mean recompense, reckoning, the professed way, obedience, or custom; its root sense is recompense.
JISHUMI:v10p7555/r10.anchor: الدين: الجزاء، والدين: الحساب، والدين: ما يدان به، والدين: الطاعة، والدين: العادة، وأصل الباب: الجزاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r1.speaker: عكرمة، مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r1.claim: Ikrima and Mujahid say the religion denied is the reckoning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r1.anchor: أحدها : يعني بالحساب , قاله عكرمة ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is God's judgment.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : بحكم الله تعالى , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r3.claim: Mawardi also allows that the religion means recompense, reward, and punishment.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say it was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r4.anchor: أحدها : أنها نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي , قاله الكلبي ومقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r5.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says it was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r5.anchor: الثاني : في الوليد بن المغيرة , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r6.claim: Another reported identification is Abu Jahl.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r7.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the person as Amr ibn Aidh.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r7.anchor: الرابع : في عمرو بن عائذ , قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it was Abu Sufyan, who slaughtered a camel but struck an orphan who asked for meat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350#2/r8.anchor: في أبي سفيان وقد نحر جزورا , فأتاه يتيم , فسأله منها , فقرعه بعصا , قاله ابن جريج .

MUQATIL:107:1-7/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r1.anchor: يعني بالحساب، نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي

MUQATIL:107:1-7/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r2.claim: The passage was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī and Hubayra ibn Abī Wahb al-Makhzūmī, husband of the Prophet's aunt Umm Hāniʾ.
MUQATIL:107:1-7/r2.anchor: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي، وهبيرة بن أبي وهب المخزومى، زوج أم هانى بنت عبدالمطلب عمة النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.claim: Most call al-Māʿūn an early Makkan sūrah after al-Takāthur, though some assign vv. 4–7 to Madinah; since the whole sūrah addresses religious hypocrisy, it may all be Madinan, when hypocrisy could gain political advantage.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r1.anchor: commentators maintain that al-Māʿūn is an early Makkan sūrah

STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.claim: Religious hypocrisy is not treated as limited to Muslims alone.
STUDYQURAN:107:intro/r2.anchor: Nonetheless, hypocrisy in religion was not seen as limited to Muslims alone.

ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.claim: The surah was revealed in the mission's early years, probably after surah 102; its title comes from al-ma'un in the last verse.
ASAD-NOTES:107:intro/r1.anchor: revealed in the early years of the Prophet's mission (probably after surah 102), is derived from the word al-ma'un occurring in the last verse

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.claim: The two groups cross-correspond: verse 1 and verses 4–6 concern religious omissions, while verses 2–3 and verse 7 concern social omissions; the first group stresses social failings and the second religious ones.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:4-7:kommentar/r4.anchor: Inhaltlich korrespondieren insofern V. 1 und V. 4–6 (religiöse Unterlassungen) und V. 2.3 und V. 7 (soziale Unterlassungen)

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.claim: The surah warns people professing religion whose traits resemble hypocrites: neglecting prayer, acting ostentatiously, and withholding aid, all incompatible with belief in requital.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r1.anchor: بيان وعيد لمن كان من المنتحلين بالدين متخلقا بأخلاق المنافقين

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.claim: The surah may be Meccan or Medinan; another view says its first half is Meccan and second half Medinan.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r2.anchor: والسورة تحتمل المكية والمدنية، وقيل نصفها مكي ونصفها مدني

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r3.claim: The seeing in the opening may be literal vision or recognition; the Prophet is addressed as a listener and thus the address extends to every listener. Here din means requital, making its denier a denier of resurrection.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r3.anchor: الرؤية تحتمل الرؤية البصرية وتحتمل أن تكون بمعنى المعرفة، والخطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r4.speaker: unnamed view
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r4.claim: Another view takes al-din here to mean religion or religious law.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r4.anchor: وقيل المراد به الدين بمعنى الملة

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r11.claim: The consequence-marker applies the denier of requital to these praying people; they display belief while practically denying requital, so they are not free of hypocrisy.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r11.anchor: وفي الآية تطبيق من يكذب بالدين على هؤلاء المصلين لمكان فاء التفريع

TABATABAI:107:1-7/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r14.claim: Al-Qummi's tafsir says the opening was revealed about Abu Jahl and the Quraysh unbelievers.
TABATABAI:107:1-7/r14.anchor: قال نزلت في أبي جهل وكفار قريش

BURSEVI:v10p403/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p403/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p403/r1.claim: The chapter is Meccan with either six or seven verses; the Prophet is asked whether he knows the one who denies recompense or Islam.

QASHANI:107:1-3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:107:1-3/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:107:1-3/r1.claim: The denier of recompense is ignorant and veiled from the disgraceful consequence; this person embodies all vices because ignorance and veiling in the rational faculty are their root.
QASHANI:107:1-3/r1.anchor: هل عرفت الجاهل المحجوب عن الجزاء من هوان لم تعرفه

QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r1.claim: Hearing the basmala nourishes lovers' spirits, lights the finders' secrets, heals repentant hearts, tests the poor, and remedies the needy.
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r1.anchor: بسم الله ' كلمة سماعها غذاء أرواح المحبين ، ضياء أسرار الواجدين ، شفاء قلوب

QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r2.claim: The verse rebukes and expresses wonder at disbelievers' abuse of orphans; religion here includes accounting and recompense.
QUSHAYRI:v3p453/r2.anchor: يكذب بالدين } . نزلت الآية على جهة التوبيخ ، والتعجب من شأن تظلم اليتيم من الكفار

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r1.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the one who denies the Judgment as an unbeliever.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r1.anchor: عن الحسن قوله : ارايت الذي يكذب بالدين قال : الكافر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets denial of the din as denial of God's judgment or rule.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3468/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : ارايت الذي يكذب بالدين قال : يكذب بحكم الله

IBNASHUR:107:1/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r1.claim: The surah is commonly called al-Māʿūn because that word occurs uniquely here; other recorded names include Araʾayta, used in some commentaries, a fifth-century Qayrawān muṣḥaf, and al-Bukhārī.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r1.anchor: في كثير من المصاحف وكتب التفسير

IBNASHUR:107:1/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR:107:1/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah titles it Sūrat Araʾayta alladhī; al-Kawāshī gives the combined title al-Māʿūn wa-l-Dīn wa-Araʾayta.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r2.anchor: وكذلك في مصحف من مصاحف القيروان في القرن الخامس

IBNASHUR:107:1/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r3.claim: Other names are Sūrat al-Dīn in al-Itqān, Sūrat al-Takdhīb in al-Khafājī and Saʿdī glosses, and Sūrat al-Yatīm in al-Biqāʿī.

IBNASHUR:107:1/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r4.claim: Most hold the surah Meccan, with a Meccan report from Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Qurṭubī transmits Qatādah’s view that it is Medinan, also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.

IBNASHUR:107:1/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r5.claim: A view attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās and stated by Hibat Allāh al-Ḍarīr assigns the first three verses to Mecca and the rest to Medina, taking the latter verses as about hypocrites; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this more apparent.

IBNASHUR:107:1/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r6.claim: On the Meccan dating, it is ranked seventeenth in revelation, after al-Takāthur and before al-Kāfirūn.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r6.anchor: وعدت السابعة عشرة في عداد نزول السور بناء على أنها مكية

IBNASHUR:107:1/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r7.claim: Most verse counters count six; al-Ālūsī says this is the Iraqi Basran and Kufan count, while ʿAlī al-Nūrī al-Ṣafāqusī reports seven for Ḥimṣ and six elsewhere, contradicting al-Ālūsī.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r7.anchor: وعدت آياتها ستا عند معظم العادين

IBNASHUR:107:1/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r8.claim: The surah exposes denial of resurrection through aggression and contempt toward the weak, withholding food from the poor, and neglect of prayer and almsgiving.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r8.anchor: من مقاصد التعجيب من حال من كذبوا بالبعث وتفظيع أعمالهم

IBNASHUR:107:1/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r9.claim: The opening question expresses astonishment at deniers and the evil conduct their denial produces; denial itself is common, so the listener waits for the surprising orphan abuse revealed next.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r9.anchor: الاستفهام مستعمل في التعجيب من حال المكذبين بالجزاء

IBNASHUR:107:1/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r10.claim: Adding the demonstrative and relative clause after fāʾ heightens suspense, then lets the description strike and firmly occupy the listener’s attention.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r10.anchor: وفي إقحام اسم الإشارة واسم الموصول بعد الفاء زيادة تشويق حتى تقرع الصلة سمع السامع فتتمكن منه

IBNASHUR:107:1/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r11.claim: The expected plain wording would directly coordinate the denial with pushing the orphan and failing to urge feeding the poor.

IBNASHUR:107:1/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r12.claim: The demonstrative singles out the denier for full recognition and inspection, or treats him as so obvious that he can be pointed at.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r12.anchor: لتمييزه أكمل تمييز حتى يتبصر السامع فيه وفي صفته

IBNASHUR:107:1/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r13.claim: The fāʾ links the second attribute to the first and makes the combined attributes support the judgment; denial, orphan abuse, and neglect of feeding are joined as one person’s qualities.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r13.anchor: لإفادة تسبب مجموع الصفتين في الحكم المقصود من الكلام

IBNASHUR:107:1/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r14.claim: This makes resurrection denial ugly through its vices and opposition to moral responsibility, warning Muslims away from either trait as characteristic of those who reject recompense.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r14.anchor: وفي ذلك كناية عن تحذير المسلمين من الاقتراب من إحدى هاتين الصفتين بأنهما من صفات الذين لا يؤمنون بالجزاء

IBNASHUR:107:1/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r15.claim: The imperfect verbs “denies,” “pushes,” and “urges” convey that the conduct is repeated and continuous.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r15.anchor: بصيغة المضارع لإفادة تكرر ذلك منه ودوامه

IBNASHUR:107:1/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r16.claim: Belief in resurrection and recompense is the true restraint that roots good conduct until it becomes a natural habit, without needing commands or fear of enforcement.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r16.anchor: وهذا إيذان بأن الإيمان بالبعث والجزاء هو الوازع الحق الذي يغرس في النفس جذور الإقبال على الأعمال الصالحة حتى يصير ذلك لها خلقا

IBNASHUR:107:1/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r17.claim: The vision is physical/visual and takes one object; famous deniers and their notorious deeds are portrayed as if visibly seen.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r17.anchor: والرؤية بصرية يتعدى فعلها إلى مفعول واحد

IBNASHUR:107:1/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r18.claim: Nāfiʿ eases the second hamza in Araʾayta into an alif; Egyptian transmitters from Warsh likewise substitute alif, as Ibn ʿĀshūr recited in Tunisia, avoiding two consecutive hamzas.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r18.anchor: وقرأ نافع بتسهيل الهمزة التي بعد الراء

IBNASHUR:107:1/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r19.claim: The majority pronounce both hamzas fully, while al-Kisāʾī drops the hamza after rāʾ in every verb of this form.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r19.anchor: وقرأه الجمهور بتحقيقهما .  وقرأه الكسائي بإسقاط الهمزة

IBNASHUR:107:1/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r20.claim: The relative pronoun and its clause refer generically to anyone with these traits, as most exegetes hold.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r20.anchor: واسم الموصول وصلته مراد بهما جنس من اتصف بذلك

IBNASHUR:107:1/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r21.claim: Some identify the occasion as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, others al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah or ʿAmr ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Makhzūmī; attribution to one person would not restrict the general ruling.

IBNASHUR:107:1/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r22.claim: Another report concerns Abū Sufyān before Islam: after he slaughtered a camel weekly, an orphan asked for its meat and he struck the child with a stick.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r22.anchor: في أبي سفيان بن حرب قبل إسلامه بسبب أنه كان ينحر كل أسبوع جزورا

IBNASHUR:107:1/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r23.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r23.claim: A report names Abū Jahl, who was guardian to an orphan; when the child came unclothed asking for his own money, Abū Jahl shoved him violently.
IBNASHUR:107:1/r23.anchor: كان وصيا على يتيم فأتاه عريانا يسأله من مال نفسه

IBNASHUR:107:1/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:107:1/r24.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:107:1/r24.claim: Those who date the surah to Medina say it concerns an unnamed hypocrite; the occasion reports are attributed in part to Successors.

TUSTARI:107:1/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:107:1/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:107:1/r1.claim: The denied religion is the reckoning on the Day when people are judged.
TUSTARI:107:1/r1.anchor: قال: أي بالحساب يوم يدان الناس.

AKHFASH:v2p586/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p586/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p586/r1.claim: Arāʾayta is read with or without the hamza; both are dialect forms, and frequent use of the word leads to hamza deletion.
AKHFASH:v2p586/r1.anchor: تحذف الهمزة لكثرة استعمال هذه الكلمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r2.claim: Sura al-Ma'un is also called Sura Ara'ayta; most say it is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r2.anchor: ويقال لها سورة أرأيت وفيها قولان أحدهما مكية قاله الجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r3.claim: Another view says Sura al-Ma'un is Medinan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r3.anchor: والثاني مدنية روى عن ابن عباس وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r4.speaker: هبة الله المفسر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r4.claim: Hibat Allah says half the surah came down in Mecca about al-As ibn Wa'il and half in Medina about the hypocrite Abd Allah ibn Ubayy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p242/r4.anchor: وقال هبة الله المفسر نزل نصفها بمكة في العاص بن وائل ونصفها بالمدينة في عبد الله بن أبي المنافق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r1.claim: One view says the verse was revealed about an unnamed hypocrite.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r1.anchor: أحدها نزلت في رجل من المنافقين قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says it was revealed about Amr ibn A'idh.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r2.anchor: والثاني نزلت في عمرو بن عائذ قاله الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says it was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r3.anchor: والثالث في الوليد بن المغيرة قاله السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r4.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib says it was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r4.anchor: والرابع في العاص بن وائل قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it was revealed about Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r5.anchor: والخامس في أبي سفيان بن حرب قاله ابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r6.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r6.claim: Al-Mawardi reports Abu Jahl as another proposed occasion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r6.anchor: والسادس في أبي جهل حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r7.claim: Al-Din can mean God's law or judgment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r7.anchor: أحدها أنه حكم الله عز وجل قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r9.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r9.claim: Al-Mawardi gives recompense as a third meaning.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p243/r10.claim: Some exegetes say al-din means the Qur'an.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p493#2/r1.claim: “The religion” denied here means resurrection, recompense, and reward.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r1.claim: One reading drops the hamza in رأيت; the author says this is not preferred because Arabic deletes it only in the imperfect, though the interrogative at the start eases it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r1.anchor: بحذف الهمزة ، وليس بالاختيار ؛ لأن حذفها مختص بالمضارع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r2.claim: A poetic line demonstrates the hamza-less form, and the opening interrogative is said to make its use easier.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r2.anchor: ولكن الذي سهل من أمرها وقوع حرف الاستفهام في أول الكلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reads أرأيتك with an added second-person marker, as in another Qurʾanic phrase.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( أرأيتك ) بزيادة حرف الخطاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r4.claim: The question means: do you know who denies requital? If not, it is the one who harshly drives away an orphan.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p808/r4.anchor: والمعنى : هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء من هو ؟ إن لم تعرفه

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350/r1.speaker: عطاء وجابر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350/r1.claim: Ata and Jabir classify Surat al-Ma'un as Meccan.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada classify it as Medinan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p350/r2.anchor: ومدينة في قول ابن عباس وقتادة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p359/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359/r1.claim: The question asks whether the listener recognizes who denies recompense, if he does not already know.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p359/r1.anchor: أى هل عرفت الذى يكذب بالجزاء من هو ان لم تعرفه

NAHHAS:v5p295/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p295/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p295/r1.claim: The standard form is clear; the hamza may be pronounced between full hamza and ease, or omitted; Ibn Masʿūd adds a kāf of address.
NAHHAS:v5p295/r1.anchor: هذه القراءة البينة ويجوز أن تأتي الهمزة بين بين فتقول أرأيت ويجوز أريت بحذف الهمزة

NAHHAS:v5p295/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p295/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
NAHHAS:v5p295/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads arāytaka, with an extra kāf for direct address.
NAHHAS:v5p295/r2.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن مسعود ( أرأيتك ) والكاف زائدة للخطاب

NAHHAS:v5p295/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p295/r3.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v5p295/r3.claim: Sībawayh says hamza between-between remains mobile at an intermediate weight; the claim that it is neither still nor mobile is impossible.
NAHHAS:v5p295/r3.anchor: همزة بين بين متحركة بوزنها مخففة كذا قال سيبويه فأما قول من قال هي لا ساكنة ولا متحركة فمحال

NAHHAS:v5p295/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p295/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p295/r4.claim: A line beginning a-an raʾat is cited for the hamza's mobility; if both hamzas were full, the meter would stay the same.
NAHHAS:v5p295/r4.anchor: والدليل على أنها متحركة قول ( أان رأت رجلا أعشى أضر به … ريب المنون

NAHHAS:v5p295/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p295/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p295/r5.claim: The phrase sawāʾ ʿalayhim a-anẓartahum also shows that a still hamza would create two adjacent sukūns; the yāʾ in arāyta is still, so the eased hamza must be mobile.
NAHHAS:v5p295/r5.anchor: ومن دليل ما قلنا قوله عز وجل

NAHHAS:v5p295/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p295/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p295/r6.claim: Those who still the eased hamza and kasra the yāʾ produce an impossible form with no Arabic analysis.
NAHHAS:v5p295/r6.anchor: ومن أسكنها وكسر الياء فقد جاء بما لا يجوز وما لا وجه له ولا تقدير في العربية

NAHHAS:v5p295/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p295/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p295/r7.claim: Arāyta may mean seeing with the eye and require no ellipsis, or seeing with the heart, with an implied question whether the denier deserves God's punishment after the proofs.
NAHHAS:v5p295/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون أرأيت من رؤية العين فلا يكون في الكلام حذف وأن يكون من رؤية القلب

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r1.claim: Religion here means requital and the accounting of the afterlife; the question omits its answer, asking whether the denier is right or mistaken.

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that the second hamza in أرأيت remains because the verb is not contracted to ريت; the interrogative hamza is softened to an alif.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r2.anchor: و { أرأيت } بإثبات الهمزة الثانية إذ لا يقال في أرأيت: ريت

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r3.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r3.claim: Abu Salih transmits from Ibn Abbas that the sūra was revealed about al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil; al-Kalbi and Muqatil agree.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r3.anchor: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits Ibn Abbas’s alternative view that it concerned one of the hypocrites.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r4.anchor: وروى الضحاك عنه قال: نزلت في رجل من المنافقين

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r5.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says the revelation concerned al-Walid ibn al-Mughira; other opinions name Abu Jahl or ʿAmr ibn ʿAʾidh.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r5.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the sūra was revealed about Abu Sufyan, who struck an orphan with his staff after the child asked him for something.
QURTUBI-FULL:107:1-5/r6.anchor: قال ابن جريج: نزلت في أبي سفيان، وكان ينحر في كل أسبوع جزورا

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r1.claim: Reports differ on dating: some call the whole surah Meccan, while others call its first three verses Meccan and the rest Medinan; Qutb calls the mixed account likelier.

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.claim: Although Qutb leans toward a wholly Medinan setting because hypocrisy and ostentation were unfamiliar in Mecca, he allows later verses to have been appended for thematic continuity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r2.anchor: وإن كانت السورة كلها وحدة متماسكة

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.claim: The seven short verses overturn conventional ideas of faith and disbelief and reveal the creed’s mercy and immense good for humanity.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r3.anchor: إن هذه السورة الصغيرة ذات الآيات السبع القصيرة تعالج حقيقة ضخمة تكاد تبدل المفهوم السائد للإيمان والكفر

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r4.claim: Religion is not outward forms or ritual; worship matters only when sincere devotion produces good deeds and sound social conduct.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r4.anchor: إن هذا الدين ليس دين مظاهر وطقوس

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.claim: Religion is an integrated way of life whose worship, rites, and personal and social duties purify hearts and lead people to cooperation, care, and flourishing.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r5.anchor: إنما هو منهج متكامل ، تتعاون عباداته وشعائره

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r6.claim: A verbal claim to Islam and performance of prayer or other rites do not prove faith; its signs must appear in the person’s conduct.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r6.anchor: ولقد يقول الإنسان بلسانه : إنه مسلم

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r7.claim: Faith, once settled in the heart, immediately moves a person to righteous action; failure to move shows that faith is absent.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r7.anchor: إن حقيقة الإيمان حين تستقر في القلب تتحرك من فورها

QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r8.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r8.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r8.claim: The opening question summons anyone able to see to identify the person who denies the Judgment.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:1/r8.anchor: إنها تبدأ بهذا الاستفهام الذي يوجه كل من تتأتى منه الرؤية ليرى

QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r1.claim: The Qur’an answers who denies the Judgment by pointing to the person who shoves the orphan and refuses care for the poor, surprising under conventional definitions of faith.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:2/r1.anchor: ومن هو هذا الذي يكذب بالدين

QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r3.claim: True assent transforms the heart and prompts kindness and care for fellow humans who need protection.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r3.anchor: إنما هي تحول في القلب يدفعه إلى الخير والبر بإخوانه

QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r4.claim: God asks for deeds that confirm words; words without confirming action are worthless before Him.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r4.anchor: إنما يريد منهم معها أعمالا تصدقها

QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r5.claim: These opening verses state with unusual clarity the spirit of the creed and the nature of the religion.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r5.anchor: وليس أصرح من هذه الآيات الثلاث في تقرير هذه الحقيقة التي تمثل روح هذه العقيدة وطبيعة هذا الدين

QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r6.claim: Qutb declines to debate juristic boundaries of faith and Islam: those govern legal transactions, while this surah states God’s measure of the underlying reality.
QUTB-ZILAL:107:3/r6.anchor: فأما هنا فالسورة تقرر حقيقة الأمر في اعتبار الله وميزانه

RAZI-FULL:v32p104/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p104/r1.claim: The chapter Al-Ma'un is Meccan and consists of seven verses.

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r1.claim: Some read أريت, deleting the hamza; al-Zajjaj considers it nonpreferred, since Arabs do not use ريت for the past, though the initial interrogative may ease deletion; a cited line supplies a parallel.

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reads أرأيتك with an added second-person suffix, as in another Quranic expression.
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود أرأيتك بزيادة حرف الخطاب

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r3.claim: Arayta asks whether the listener knows who denies the recompense; if not, the answer is the one who pushes away the orphan.
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r3.anchor: معناه هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء من هو

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r4.claim: Though phrased as a question, the expression intensifies amazement, like asking what someone has done and why he exposed himself to danger.
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r4.anchor: اللفظ وإن كان في صورة الاستفهام

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r5.claim: The address may be to the Prophet, or to every rational person: why knowingly incur eternal punishment after clear proofs, or trade the lasting great for fleeting worldly gain?
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r5.anchor: إنه خطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it was revealed about Abu Sufyan, who slaughtered two camels weekly but struck an orphan who asked him for meat.
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r6.anchor: نزلت في أبي سفيان كان ينحر جزورين في كل أسبوع

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r7.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r7.claim: Maqatil says it was revealed about al-Asi ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, who combined denial of Judgment with ugly deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r7.anchor: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r8.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi identifies al-Walid ibn al-Mughira as the person concerned.

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r9.speaker: الماوردي
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r9.claim: Al-Mawardi reports that the verse concerned Abu Jahl, a ward’s guardian who rejected the naked orphan’s request for his own property; Muhammad accompanied him to Abu Jahl, who relented out of fear of spears he imagined beside the Prophet.
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r9.anchor: حكى الماوردي أنها نزلت في أبي جهل

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about a hypocrite who combined stinginess and ostentation.
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r10.anchor: وروى عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في منافق جمع بين البخل والمراءاة

RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r11.claim: The verse is general to every denier of Judgment: belief in resurrection drives obedience and restraint, while denial removes that restraint and underlies sins and disbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v32p104#2/r11.anchor: أنه عام لكل من كان مكذبا بيوم الدين

RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r1.claim: One interpretation is denial of religion or Islam, including denial of God, prophethood, resurrection, or any revealed law.
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r1.anchor: أن يكون المراد من يكذب بنفس الدين والإسلام إما لأنه كان منكرا للصانع

RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r2.claim: Although everyone follows some creed, unqualified din in Islamic usage means Islam; other creeds are named only with a qualifier such as the religion of Christians or Jews.
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r2.anchor: الدين المطلق في اصطلاح أهل الإسلام

RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r3.claim: Another answer is that false doctrines are not truly religion, which means submission to God; they amount instead to submission to passion or conjecture.
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r3.anchor: أن الدين هو الخضوع لله وهذه المذاهب إنما هي خضوع للشهوة أو للشبهة

RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r4.claim: Most commentators interpret din as accounting and recompense; Razi prefers this because someone who affirms resurrection may reject Islam yet still do good, whereas reckless wrongdoing points to denying resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v32p105/r4.anchor: وحمله على هذا الوجه أولى لأن من ينكر الإسلام

STUDYQURAN:107:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r1.speaker: Muqātil and al-Kalbī
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r1.claim: They say the surah was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī.
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r1.anchor: Muqātil and al-Kalbī said, “This sūrah was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī”

STUDYQURAN:107:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r2.speaker: Ibn Jurayj
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abū Sufyān struck with a stick an orphan who asked him for something while he was slaughtering his weekly camels, prompting revelation.
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r2.anchor: Ibn Jurayj said, “Abū Sufyān was in the habit

STUDYQURAN:107:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r3.claim: Even if first tied to one person, the accusation has general force; denying dīn, as religion or Judgment, underlies other sins and violations.
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r3.anchor: Even if it was first recorded in reference to a specific individual, it still has a general implication

STUDYQURAN:107:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r4.claim: Dīn can mean religion or judgment, including denial of Resurrection and the Afterlife.
STUDYQURAN:107:1/r4.anchor: Dīn could also mean “judgment” and relate to the denial of the Resurrection and other events of the Afterlife

SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r1.speaker: الكسائي
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r1.claim: Al-Kisai reads arayta without the hamza; al-Zamakhshari says this is not preferred because deletion is confined to imperfect verbs and riʾtu is unattested, though initial questioning eased it as in poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " وليس بالاختيار؛ لأن حذفها مختص بالمضارع، ولم يصح عن العرب " ريت

SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r2.claim: One reading takes arayta as visual perception, governing one object, the relative clause: did you see the denier?
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r2.anchor: وفي " أرأيت " هذه وجهان، أحدهما: أنها بصرية فتتعدى لواحد وهو الموصول

SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r3.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r3.claim: For the tell-me reading, al-Hawfi estimates the second object as whether the denier deserves punishment.

SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r4.claim: For the tell-me reading, al-Zamakhshari estimates the second object as who the denier is.

SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r5.claim: Abd Allah's araytaka reading with an addressee kaf supports the sense tell me, since visual raʾayta does not take that kaf.
SAMIN-DURR:107:1/r5.anchor: ويدل على ذلك قراءة عبد الله " أرأيتك " بكاف الخطاب والكاف لا تلحق البصرية

TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r1.claim: The denier of the dīn denies God's reward and punishment, so does not obey His commands and prohibitions.
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r1.anchor: وعقابه، فلا يطيعه في أمره ونهيه.

TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses dīn as God's judgment or ordinance.
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين} [الماعون: 1] قال: «الذي يكذب بحكم الله عز وجل»

TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses dīn as the reckoning.

TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r4.claim: In ʿAbd Allāh's reading, the phrase lacks the bāʾ; al-Ṭabarī says the preposition makes no difference to the sense.
TAB-FULL:v24p657#2/r4.anchor: وذكر أن ذلك في قراءة عبد الله: «أرأيت الذي يكذب الدين» فالباء في قراءته صلة،

ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r1.claim: The preferred reading keeps the second hamza in araʾayta; deleting it is easier at the start of a question, but rītu is not attested from Arabs for رأيت.
ZAJJAJ:v5p367/r1.anchor: والاختيار أرأيت بإثبات الهمزة الثانية لأن الهمزة إنما طرحت للمستقبل في ترى ويرى وأرى

THALABI:v10p304#3/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r1.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
THALABI:v10p304#3/r1.claim: They identify the person denounced as al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي،

THALABI:v10p304#3/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r2.speaker: السدي ومقاتل بن حيان وابن كيسان
THALABI:v10p304#3/r2.claim: They say the verse concerns al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r2.anchor: السدي ومقاتل بن حيان وابن كيسان: يعني الوليد بن المغيرة،

THALABI:v10p304#3/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r3.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v10p304#3/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the person as Amr ibn A'id ibn Imran ibn Makhzum.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r3.anchor: الضحاك: في عمرو بن عائد بن عمران بن مخزوم،

THALABI:v10p304#3/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p304#3/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p304#3/r4.claim: Another identification given is Haybara ibn Abi Wahb al-Makhzumi.
THALABI:v10p304#3/r4.anchor: وقيل: هيبرة بن أبي وهب المخزومي،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq prefers retaining the second hamza in arayta: it drops in imperfect forms, not the perfect; an initial interrogative alif can ease its omission, but retention is preferable.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r1.anchor: - {أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين} قال أبو إسحاق: الاختيار (أرأيت) بإثبات الهمزة الثانية، لأن الهمزة إنما طرحت من المستقبل نحو: ترى، وأرى، ويرى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r2.claim: “Have you seen the one who…” draws attention to the condition of the person described as denying the Judgment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r2.anchor: التنبيه على حال المخبر عنه بالتكذيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports Ibn ʿAbbās saying the sūra was revealed about a hypocrite.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r3.anchor: قال (عطاء عن) (¬1) ابن عباس: نزلت (¬2) في رجل من المنافقين (¬3)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies the subject as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r4.anchor: وقال الكلبي: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي (¬4).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r5.speaker: السدي وابن حيان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī and Ibn Ḥayyān identify him as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r5.anchor: (وقال السدي (¬5)، وابن حيان (¬6): يعني الوليد بن المغيرة) (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says dīn here means reckoning and recompense.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r7.claim: The people of linguistic interpretation say denying recompense is especially harmful because it removes incentives to do good and restraints from evil, leaving no fear of return harm or hope of reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p355#2/r7.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: التكذيب بالجزاء أضر شيء على صاحبه؛ لأنه # يعدم به أكثر الدواعي إلى الخير، والصوارف عن الشر؛ لأنه لا يخاف عائد الضر، ولا يرجو (¬1) الجزاء على الخير

WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r1.speaker: العاص بن وائل
WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r1.claim: One report identifies al-As ibn Wa'il as the occasion of revelation.

WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r2.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r2.claim: Another report identifies al-Walid ibn al-Mughira as the occasion.
WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r2.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r3.speaker: أبو سفيان
WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r3.claim: A third report says Abu Sufyan slaughtered a camel, then drove off an orphan who came asking, striking him with a stick.
WAHIDI-QT:107:1/r3.anchor: وذلك أنه نحر جزورا فأتاه يتيم يسأله ،   فقرعه بعصاه

ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n1/r1.claim: Asad reads din as objective validity of religion and moral law.
ASAD-NOTES:107:1#n1/r1.anchor: objective validity in religion as such

ELMALILI:107:1/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:1/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:1/r1.claim: The address is to the Prophet and, by implication, anyone able to receive the address; the question is an expression of wonder meant to draw attention.
ELMALILI:107:1/r1.anchor: Hitab yine Resûlullah’a ve dolayısıyla umûmen hitâba kābiliyeti olanların her birinedir

ELMALILI:107:1/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:1/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:1/r2.claim: Seeing people depend on mutual aid amid hunger, satiety, fear, and safety makes denial of divine recompense astonishing; the question exposes deniers’ character and warns believers against it.
ELMALILI:107:1/r2.anchor: Hak teâlâ’nın cezâ ve mükâfâtını inkâr edenlerin, dine inanmayanların bulunması taaccüb edilecek bir şey olduğuna tenbih

ELMALILI:107:1/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:1/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:1/r3.claim: Dīn here means recompense: God certainly rewards good and punishes evil, so people will encounter what they did; this is a binding truth to affirm and obey.
ELMALILI:107:1/r3.anchor: Burada da “dîn” en mutlak ve en esaslı mefhûmu olan ceza mânasınadır

ELMALILI:107:1/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:1/r4.speaker: Mukātil
ELMALILI:107:1/r4.claim: Muqātil reports that the verse was revealed about ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil al-Sahmī, who denied the Resurrection and acted immorally.
ELMALILI:107:1/r4.anchor: Mukātil’den bunun Âs b. Vâil-i Sehmî hakkında nâzil olduğu rivayet edilmiş

ELMALILI:107:1/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:1/r5.speaker: Süddî
ELMALILI:107:1/r5.claim: Al-Suddī reports that it was revealed about al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra.
ELMALILI:107:1/r5.anchor: Süddî’den Velid b. Mugīre hakkında nâzil olduğu rivayet edilmiş

ELMALILI:107:1/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:1/r6.speaker: Mâverdî
ELMALILI:107:1/r6.claim: Al-Māwardī transmits that it was revealed about Abū Jahl; a report says he had charge of an orphan, shoved him away when he came destitute asking for his own property, then gave it after the Prophet accompanied him.
ELMALILI:107:1/r6.anchor: Mâverdî de Ebû Cehil hakkında nâzil olduğunu nakleylemiş

ELMALILI:107:1/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:1/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:1/r7.claim: In the orphan account, Quraysh mocked Abū Jahl for giving in; he said two spears appeared beside the Prophet and he feared being struck if he refused.
ELMALILI:107:1/r7.anchor: velâkin onun sağında solunda birer harbe gördüm, vermezsem vuracak diye korktum

ELMALILI:107:1/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:1/r8.speaker: İbni Abbas
ELMALILI:107:1/r8.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse concerns a hypocrite who is both miserly and ostentatious.
ELMALILI:107:1/r8.anchor: İbni Abbas’tan bir rivayette de hem bahil hem mürâî bir münafık hakkında nazil oldu denilmiştir

ELMALILI:107:1/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:107:1/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:107:1/r9.claim: The sūra may have been revealed for one or all of these people, but its ruling applies to everyone like them.
ELMALILI:107:1/r9.anchor: fakat hükmü onlara mahsus değil, öylelerin hepsine şâmildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r1.claim: The question asking whether one has seen something flags an astonishing attitude and signals the importance of the topic.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r1.anchor: “Gördün mü?” sorusu, burada şaşılacak bir tutumdan söz edileceğine, dolayısıyla konunun önemli olduğuna dikkat çekmeyi amaçlamaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r2.claim: Din can mean God's judgment or judgment in the afterlife as well as its familiar senses; denying one entails denying the others, so the result is the same.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r2.anchor: “Allah’ın hükmü” veya “uhrevî yargı” mânasında da anlaşılabilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r3.claim: Most exegetes understand din here as recompense, punishment, and reward; verses 2–3 then portray people who do not fear mistreating orphans or neglecting the poor because they deny an afterlife reckoning.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r3.anchor: Müfessirlerin çoğunluğu buradaki “din” kelimesiyle bu anlamın kastedildiğini belirtmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur says the broader purpose is to condemn cruelty and injustice as grave evils rooted in denial of religion, God's judgments, or afterlife responsibility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:107:1/r5.anchor: bu tür kaba ve haksız davranışları sergileyenleri kınamak ve bu yaptıklarının Allah katında en büyük kötülüklerden olduğuna

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r1.claim: Mujahid and al-Kalbi say the opening about one who denies Judgment and repulses the orphan was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل والكلبي: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abu Sufyan slaughtered two camels each week; when an orphan asked him for food, he struck the child with a stick, and the verses were revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p465#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: كان أبو سفيان بن حرب ينحر كل أسبوع جزورين

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r1.claim: The rhetorical phrase ʾa-raʾaita is compared with its repeated use in 96:9–13 and with 53:33–34.

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r2.claim: The commentary directs readers to notes on other uses of kaḏḏaba in 95:7, 92:16, and 73:11.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Zu den verschiedenen Gebrauchsweisen von kaḏḏaba vgl. die Anmerkungen zu 95:7, 92:16 und 73:11

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r3.claim: Early Meccan dīn and yawm al-dīn are objects of belief or denial, supporting the received bi-d-dīn reading over Ibn Masʿūd’s variant without bi.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Ad-dīn bzw. yaum ad-dīn erscheinen frühmekkanisch vor allem als Gegenstand des Glaubens

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r4.speaker: Birkeland
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r4.claim: Birkeland proposes that dīn means religion here rather than judgment, but the author rejects this because dīn and yawm al-dīn are synonymous prepositional objects of kaḏḏaba in Quranic usage.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Birkelands Hypothese, dīn werde in 107:1 nicht in der Bedeutung von „Gericht“

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r5.claim: The author concludes that early Meccan dīn generally means judgment, against Nöldeke and Schwally’s apparent translation as religion.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Dīn dürfte deshalb frühmekkanisch generell mit „Gericht“ zu übersetzen sein

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r6.speaker: Birkeland
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r6.claim: Birkeland argues judgment would not fit because Muhammad still joined pre-Islamic Meccan prayer, but the author says cult separation could have followed the establishment of judgment themes.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r6.anchor: Auch Birkelands Gedanke, dass in Q 107 die Bedeutung „Gericht“ noch nicht sinnvoll sei

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r7.claim: Dīn later means religion, as in 109:6; its early eschatological sense reflects Aramaic dīnā, while interference from Middle Persian dēn later supplied the religious sense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r7.anchor: Der Hintergrund für diese Bedeutungsverschiebung ist in der komplexen Etymologie des Wortes zu suchen

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r8.claim: The shift was not purely linguistic: judgment receded as a comprehensive religious system developed, allowing the Quranic word to take on the Persian-influenced sense of religion.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r8.anchor: Denn das koranische Wort dīn konnte nach seiner zunächst ausschließlich eschatologischen Verwendung wohl nur deshalb überhaupt

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r9.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r9.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r9.claim: A probably authentic poem by Umayya b. Abī al-Ṣalt already uses dīn to mean religion, so Persian influence did not introduce that sense as a lexical innovation in Medinan suras.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1:anmerkung/r9.anchor: Ein interessantes Schlaglicht auf die vorkoranische Semantik von dīn ergibt sich aus einem wahrscheinlich authentischen Gedicht Umayya b. abī ṣ-Ṣalts

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura systematically links religious beliefs and ritual actions with an individual’s moral conduct in daily life.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die Sure etabliert systematisch einen Konnex zwischen religiösen Überzeugungen und kultischen Handlungen

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r2.claim: The first group uses a question introduced by ʾa-raʾaita to elicit the listener’s position on deniers of judgment, perhaps addressing worshippers who themselves observe the conduct in verses 4–5.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r2.anchor: Die erste Versgruppe tut dies in Form einer mit ʾa-raʾaita eingeleiteten Frage

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r4.claim: Awareness of the eschaton grounds social solidarity, a theme also found in 92:5–9; 104:1–3 depicts conduct when this eschatological awareness is absent.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r4.anchor: V. 1–3 stellen damit die beständige Gewärtigung des eschaton als Voraussetzung gesellschaftlicher Solidarität dar

CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r5.claim: This future-oriented accountability complements 106’s past-oriented grounding of present ethics in God’s earlier favors.
CORPUSCORANICUM:107:1-3:kommentar/r5.anchor: komplementiert die Vergangenheitsorientierung der früheren Sure 106

QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#1/r1.claim: Dropping hamza softens the interrogative opening without changing meaning; readers differ on its realization.
QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#1/r1.anchor: The hamza elision softens the interrogative opening but does not change meaning

QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#2/r1.claim: Madd lengthens the vowel in place of hamza, making the interrogative opening smoother and more sustained.
QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#2/r1.anchor: The elongated vowel replaces the glottal stop, creating a smoother but more sustained interrogative opening

QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#3/r1.claim: Tashīl softens hamza between full realization and elision, an intermediate form among the Seven readers.
QIRAAT-ER:107:1:1#3/r1.anchor: the hamza is softened between full realization and complete elision

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن الزبير والجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#2/r7.claim: The following surah is also called Araʾayta, al-Din, or al-Takdhib; most call it Meccan, while reports give a Medinan setting, and Hibat Allah says half concerns ʿAs ibn Waʾil in Mecca and half ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy in Medina.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#2/r7.anchor: وتسمى سورة أرأيت والدين والتكذيب وهي مكية في قول الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#2/r8.claim: It has seven verses in the Iraqi count and six elsewhere; its rebuke follows Quraysh’s mention of feeding the hungry, worshiping the Kaaba, and disbelief in resurrection and judgment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#2/r8.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه في سورة قريش أطعمهم من جوع ذم عز وجل هنا من لم يحض على طعام المسكين

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r1.claim: The question draws hearers to identify the denier, a matter believers must know to avoid his conduct, and also expresses wonder.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r1.anchor: استفهام أريد به تشويق السامع إلى تعرف المكذب وان ذلك مما يجب على المتدين ليحترز عنه وعن فعله وفيه أيضا تعجيب منه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r2.claim: The address may be to the Messenger or to anyone fit to receive it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r2.anchor: والخطاب لرسول الله صلى تعالى عليه وسلم أو لكل من يصلح له

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r3.claim: Here seeing means knowing, and it takes one object.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r4.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r4.claim: Al-Hawfi allows the verb to mean visual seeing; on either analysis it can figuratively mean tell me, with the relative as one object and an omitted second object such as who he is or whether he deserves punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r4.anchor: وقال الحوفي يجوز أن تكون بصرية وعلى الوجهين يجوز أن يتجوز بذلك عن الاخبار فيكون المراد بأرأيت أخبرني

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r5.claim: The author questions the rule that figurative vision must be visual vision.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r5.anchor: والقول بأنه لاتكون الرؤية المتجوز بها الا بصرية فيه نظر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r6.claim: The author also rejects an absolute ban on attaching the address kāf to visual seeing, since figurative use removes the obstacle.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r6.anchor: وكذا اطلاق القول بان كاف الخطاب لاتلحق البصرية اذ لامانع من ذلك بعد التجوز

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r7.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r7.claim: A reading attributed to Abd Allah adds an emphatic address kāf to the verb.
