ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r7.anchor: قراءة عبد الله أرأيتك بكاف الخطاب المزيدة لتأكيد التاء

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r8.claim: Al-dīn here means recompense, one of its established senses, as in the saying that one is repaid as one acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r8.anchor: والدين الجزاء وهو أحد معانيه ومنه كما تدين تدان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r10.claim: Other explanations give al-dīn as Islam, the Qur'an, or God's command; Islam is the more familiar interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r10.anchor: كما هو الاشهر ولعله من فسره بالقرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r11.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r11.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads arayta, dropping the hamza; the author explains this by analogy with regular hamza deletion in the present tense, aided by the interrogative hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r11.anchor: وقرأ الكسائى أريت بحذف الهمزة كأنه حمال الماضي في حذف همزته على مضارعه المطرد فيه حذفها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r12.claim: The interrogative hamza makes this deletion easier and gives the reading a stronger rationale than the cited poetic analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r12.anchor: ومن هنا كانت هذه القراءة أقوى توجيها مما في قوله صاح هل رأيت أو سمعت براع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r13.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r13.claim: Another account derives the reading by analogy with the past form after an interrogative hamza, but the author finds this explanation unpersuasive.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p241#3/r13.anchor: وليس بذاك وان زعم انه الاوجه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r1.claim: Muqatil identifies the denier of requital as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r2.speaker: السدي ومقاتل بن حيان وابن كيسان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī, Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān, and Ibn Kaysān identify him as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r2.anchor: وقال السدي ومقاتل بن حيان وابن كيسان: في الوليد بن المغيرة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies him as ʿAmr ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Makhzūmī.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r3.anchor: قال الضحاك: في [عمرو] (3) بن عائذ المخزومي.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ, identifies the denier as an unnamed hypocrite.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r4.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: في رجل من المنافقين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p549#2/r5.claim: The word dīn here means requital and reckoning.

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r1.claim: Araʾayta is an interrogative of astonishment; it is read arayta without hamza by analogy with the imperfect, and the initial interrogative may ease its form; araʾaytaka adds the kāf.
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r1.anchor: عناه التعجب، وقرىء «أريت» بلا همز إلحاقا بالمضارع

BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r2.claim: Al-din may mean requital or Islam, and the relative expression may be generic or refer to a known person; the following verse supports the latter.
BAYDAWI-FULL:107:1-5/r2.anchor: بالجزاء أو الإسلام والذي يحتمل الجنس والعهد ويؤيد الثاني

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r1.claim: The surah is early Makkan, follows al-Takāthur, and is seventeenth in the commonly reported revelation order.
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r1.anchor: السورة مكية مبكرة، نزلت بعد التكاثر.

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r2.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r2.claim: Al-Tabari's Jāmiʿ al-Bayān calls it Sūrat Araʾayta.
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r2.anchor: وجاءت باسم سورة "أرأيت" في جامع البيان للطبري

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's al-Kashshāf calls it Sūrat Araʾayta.

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r4.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r4.claim: Al-Razi's al-Tafsīr al-kabīr also calls it Sūrat Araʾayta.

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r5.speaker: الجمهور
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r5.claim: The majority read the opening as araʾayta, with the hamza retained.

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r6.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r6.claim: Some readers pronounce arayta, deleting the hamza from raʾā; al-Zamakhshari considers this nonpreferred because deletion is normally limited to the imperfect and ريت is unattested, though the initial interrogative may ease it.
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r6.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم "أريتَ" بحذف الهمزة من رأى، قال في الكشاف: "وليس بالاختيار

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r7.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari cites a poetic line with ريت after an interrogative as a parallel for the unusual form.
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r7.anchor: صاح هل ريت أو سمعت براع رد في الضرع ما قرى في العلاب

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r8.claim: One reported occasion of revelation identifies Abu Sufyan.
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r8.anchor: وقالوا في أسباب النزول، إنها نزلت في: أبي سفيان،

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r9.claim: Another reported occasion of revelation identifies al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī.

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r10.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r10.claim: Another reported occasion of revelation identifies al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r11.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r11.claim: Another reported occasion of revelation identifies Abū Jahl.

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r12.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it was revealed about a hypocrite combining miserliness and ostentation.
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: "نزلت في منافق جمع بين البخل والمراءاة".

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r13.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r13.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r13.claim: Whatever the reported occasion, the lesson follows the general wording.
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r13.anchor: والعبرة على كل حال بعموم اللفظ

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r14.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r14.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r14.claim: The normal question seeks information the asker lacks; when the asker already knows, the interrogative shifts from its literal linguistic meaning into rhetorical figurative use.
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r14.anchor: أما حين يكون المستفهم على علم بما يستفهم عنه، فإن الاستفهام يخرج بذلك عن أصل معناه

BINTSHATI:v2p183/r15.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r15.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v2p183/r15.claim: Al-Raghib says araʾayta functions like akhbirnī, 'tell me,' and that every Qur'anic instance carries an alerting sense.

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r1.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r1.claim: Al-Razi says the purpose is to intensify astonishment.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r1.anchor: قال الفخر الرازي فيه: "إن الغرض منه المبالغة في التعجب"

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r2.speaker: محمد عبده
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r2.claim: Muhammad Abdu says the purpose is to alert people to something obscure and unknown.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r2.anchor: وذهب الشيخ محمد عبده إلى "أن المقصود به التنبيه إلى خفى مجهول".

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r3.claim: The author sees the rhetorical secret in asking about what people think is obvious: a surprising question sharpens attention for an unexpected account of what denying religion means.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r3.anchor: وأميل إلى القول بأن سره البياني فس الاستفهام عما يبدو للناس واضحاً غير خفي، ويحسبونه معلوماً غير مجهول،

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r4.claim: People often assume that professing the creed and performing obligatory worship suffice to show belief in religion.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r4.anchor: والناس يحسبونه أنه يكفي المرء تصديق بالدين لأن ينطق الشهادتين ويؤدي العبادات المفروضة

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r5.claim: In Arabic dīn means obedience and submission; the servant is called madīn because servitude subjects him, while dayyān can mean subduer, judge, or ruler.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r5.anchor: والدين في العربية: الطاعة والخضوع. وسمى العبد مديناً لأن العبودية أخضعته.

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r6.claim: Dīn commonly means a religious community or religion, especially Islam, the predominant Qur'anic sense, as in the cited verses.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r6.anchor: وشاع استعماله في الملة بعامة، وفي الإسلام بوجه خاص، وهو المعنى الغالب في الاستعمال القرآني.

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r7.claim: The expression yawm al-dīn refers to the Last Day fourteen times in the Qur'an.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r7.anchor: وسمى اليوم الآخر "يوم الدين" أربع عشرة مرة.

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r8.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r8.claim: Al-Tabari interprets dīn here as God's reward and punishment.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r8.anchor: وفي آية {أَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي يُكَذِّبُ بِالدِّينِ} فسر الدين بأنه ثواب الله وعقابه (الطبري)

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r9.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhshari likewise interprets dīn as recompense.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r9.anchor: واختار الزمخشري كذلك أن يكون بمعنى الجزاء

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r10.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r10.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r10.anchor: والأولى عند الرازي أن يكون بمعنى الإسلام

BINTSHATI:v2p184/r11.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r11.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r11.claim: The author finds the views close but prefers dīn as religious belief and Islam over reckoning or recompense, since denial of the latter entails denial of religion.
BINTSHATI:v2p184/r11.anchor: وهي أقوال متقاربة، وإن يكن حمله على الدين بمعنى العقيدة والإسلام، أقوى

BINTSHATI:v2p185/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r1.claim: Arabic kadhib covers false appearances and failed expectations (such as a camel thought pregnant or lightning mistaken for rain), sensory error, false dreams or hopes, and self-delusion; kadhdhab bi means deny or disbelieve.
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r1.anchor: والكذب: نقيض الصدق. استعملته العربية ف الناقة الكذوب يظن أنها حامل ثم تخلف الظن،

BINTSHATI:v2p185/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r2.claim: Qur'anic denial most often concerns God, His signs, and His messengers, and extends to denying the warnings, Resurrection, meeting God, the afterlife, Judgment Day, Hell, and punishment.
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r2.anchor: يأتي التكذيب في القرآن الكريم أكثر ما يأتي في التكذيب بالله وآياته ورسله

BINTSHATI:v2p185/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p185/r3.claim: The Qur'an mentions denial of dīn in al-Infiṭār, al-Tīn, and this opening verse.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.claim: Al-Māʿūn is also called al-Dīn, Araʾayta and al-Takdhīb; its central warning is that denial of resurrection and recompense is the root of vices and contempt for sacred matters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r1.anchor: مقصودها التنبيه على أن التكذيب بالبعث لأجل الجزاء أبو الخبائث ، فإنه يجزئ المكذب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r2.claim: The four names plainly signal the surah's subject: it explicitly forbids vices and implicitly urges noble conduct.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r2.anchor: وكل من اسمائها الأربعة في غاية الظهور في الدلالة على ذلك بتأمل السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r3.claim: The basmala praises God's perfection, His universal mercy to good and bad, and His special completion of grace for His allies through the joy of communion.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p541/r3.anchor: الذي تعالت عظمته عن كل شائبة نقص فكان له كل كمال { الرحمن } الذي عمت نعمته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.claim: Harshness to orphans, failure to encourage feeding the poor, neglect of prayer, ostentation and withholding help all mark denial of judgment; belief instead produces praised conduct, so believers must avoid these traits.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r1.anchor: إن هذه كلها من شأن المكذب بالحساب والجزاء لأن نفع البعد عنها إنما يكون إذ ذاك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r4.claim: Hidden deniers are exposed by behavioral signs that arise from disbelief, even when they try to conceal their inner state.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p542/r4.anchor: عرفهم بأمارات تنشأ من عمود الكفر الذي صدر به ويتفرع منه تفضحهم

DURR-FULL:v8p641/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and, in a parallel report, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr say the surah was revealed in Mecca.
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أنزلت {أرأيت الذي يكذب} بمكة وأخرج ابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن الزبير مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p641/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r2.claim: Al-Hasan glosses the one who denies the religion or judgment as the disbeliever.
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r2.anchor: عن الحسن {أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين} قال: الكافر

DURR-FULL:v8p641/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj reads al-din here as the reckoning.
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج {أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين} قال: بالحساب

DURR-FULL:v8p641/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets al-din as God’s judgment or command.
DURR-FULL:v8p641/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس {أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين} قال: يكذب بحكم الله

TAB:107:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:1/r1.speaker: author
TAB:107:1/r1.claim: The question asks about one who denies God's reward and punishment and therefore does not obey His commands or prohibitions.
TAB:107:1/r1.anchor: أرأيت يا محمد الذي يكذب بثواب الله وعقابه ،   فلا يطيعه في أمره ونهيه

TAB:107:1/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:1/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:107:1/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses denying the dīn as denying God's judgment.
TAB:107:1/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   في قوله :  {  أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين } قال :  الذي يكذب بحكم الله عز وجل

TAB:107:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:1/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB:107:1/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses al-dīn as the reckoning.
TAB:107:1/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج {  يكذب بالدين } قال :  بالحساب

TAB:107:1/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:1/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB:107:1/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading omits the preposition bāʾ from “denies the dīn.”
TAB:107:1/r4.anchor: وذُكر أن ذلك في قراءة عبد الله :  «أرأيت الذي يكذب الدين »

TAB:107:1/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:107:1/r5.speaker: author
TAB:107:1/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the bāʾ in the received reading is an added particle, so including or omitting it does not change the sense.
TAB:107:1/r5.anchor: فالباء في قراءته صلة ،   دخولها في الكلام وخروجها واحد

BAQILLANI:v1p52/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r3.speaker: أبو نواس
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r3.claim: Abu Nuwas recasts the al-Māʿūn lines in al-khafīf, changing the phrase to فذاك الذي as he fits them into his poem.
BAQILLANI:v1p52/r3.anchor: ضمنه أبو نواس في شعره ففصل وقال فذاك الذي وشعره

BURHAN:v2p114/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.claim: The section asks about Qur’anic phrases that coincide with metrical poetry, whether a full line, several lines, or a hemistich, while treating such coincidence as distinct from poetry.
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.anchor: فإن قيل فقد وجد فى القرآن ما وافق شعرا موزونا إما بيت تام أو أبيات أو مصراع

BURHAN:v2p114/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r7.speaker: قالوا
BURHAN:v2p114/r7.claim: They say the opening of al-Maʿun scans in khafif.
BURHAN:v2p114/r7.anchor: ﴿ أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم ﴾ قالوا هو من الخفيف

BURHAN:v4p151/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p151/r1.speaker: ابن خروف
BURHAN:v4p151/r1.claim: Ibn Khuruf says jurists use arāʾayta with an implicit hypothetical condition, followed by a question whose clause is suspended from governing action, like the Quranic pattern.
BURHAN:v4p151/r1.anchor: قال ابن خروف إلا أنهم يلجئون فيها وجوابها أرايت إن كان كذا وكذا كيف يكون كذا

ITQAN:v3p283/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p283/r3.speaker: أبو شامة
ITQAN:v3p283/r3.claim: Abu Shama identifies interrogative openings in six sūras, including ʿamma yatasaʾalūn, hal atā, and alam nashraḥ.
ITQAN:v3p283/r3.anchor: الثامن الاستفهام في ست سور عم يتساءلون هل أتاك ألم نشرح ألم تر أرأيت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r1.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r1.claim: The fifth Qurʾanic sense of dīn is judgment, as in the king’s law that kept Joseph from taking his brother.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r1.anchor: والخامس : الحكم . ومنه قوله تعالى : [ في يوسف ﴿ ما كان ليأخذ أخاه في دين الملك ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r2.claim: Dīn can mean obedience; Ibn Qutayba explains the phrase about not following the true dīn as not obeying it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r2.anchor: والسادس : الطاعة . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة التوبة : ﴿ ولا يدينون دين الحق ﴾ . وقال ابن قتيبة : لا يطيعونه .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r3.claim: Dīn can mean customary practice, as in the rebuke asking whether people would teach God their dīn.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r3.anchor: والسابع : العادة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحجرات : ﴿ قل أتعلمون الله بدينكم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r4.claim: Dīn can mean religious community or creed; dīn al-qayyima is glossed as the upright religion.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r4.anchor: والثامن : الملة . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في لم يكن ] : ﴿ وذلك دين القيمة ﴾ ، أي : وذلك دين الملة المستقيمة .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r5.claim: Dīn can mean prescribed legal penalties, as in the command not to let pity weaken God’s law.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r5.anchor: والتاسع : الحدود . ومنه قوله تعالى في النور : ^ ( ولا نأخذكم بهما رأفة في دين الله ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r6.claim: Dīn can mean a number; dīn al-qayyim here means the correct number of sacred months.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r6.anchor: والعاشر : العدد . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة التوبة : ﴿ منها أربعة حرم ذلك الدين القيم ﴾ ، أي : العدد الصحيح .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r7.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r7.claim: Some add an eleventh sense, the Qurʾan, citing the question about the one who denies the dīn.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p298/r7.anchor: وقد ألحق بعضهم وجها حادي عشر فقال : والدين : القرآن . ومنه قوله تعالى : ﴿ أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين ﴾

NASHR:v2p404/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p404/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p404/r5.claim: Ibn al-Jazari points back to his discussions of the hamza in أرأيت and شانئك and imāla in عابدون and عابد.
NASHR:v2p404/r5.anchor: وتقدم أرأيت وشانئك في الهمز المفرد، وتقدم عابدون وعابد في الإمالة

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r1.claim: The majority call Sūrat al-Māʿūn Meccan; Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda call it Medinan.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية في قول الجمهور ،   مدنية في قول ابن عباس وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r2.speaker: هبة الله المفسر الضرير
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r2.claim: Hibat Allāh al-Mufassir al-Ḍarīr says half the sūra came in Mecca about al-ʿĀṣī ibn Wāʾil and half in Medina about the hypocrite ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r2.anchor: قال هبة الله المفسر الضرير : نزل نصفها بمكة في العاصي بن وائل ،   ونصفها بالمدينة في عبد الله بن أبي المنافق

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r3.claim: After recounting God’s favors to Quraysh, who denied resurrection and recompense, the sūra warns them of requital and punishment.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r3.anchor: ولما عدد تعالى نعمه على قريش ،   وكانوا لا يؤمنون بالبعث والجزاء ،   اتبع امتنانه عليهم بتهديدهم بالجزاء وتخويفهم من عذابه

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r4.claim: The verse is variously said to concern Abū Jahl, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, al-ʿĀṣī ibn Wāʾil, ʿUmar ibn ʿĀʾidh, two hypocrites, or Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r4.anchor: ونزلت في أبي جهل ،   أو الوليد بن المغيرة ،   أو العاصي بن وائل ،   أو عمر بن عائذ ،   أو رجلين من المنافقين ،   أو أبي سفيان بن حرب

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj’s occasion report says Abū Sufyān sacrificed a camel weekly; when an orphan asked for something, he rebuffed the child with a stick.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r5.anchor: كان ينحر في كل أسبوع جزوراً ،   فأتاه يتيم فسأله شيئاً فقرعه بعصا ،   أقوال آخرها لابن جريج

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r6.claim: Arayta most likely means akhbirnī, takes two objects, and leaves the second understood; al-Ḥawfī estimates it as “is he not deserving of God’s punishment?”
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r6.anchor: الظاهر أن { أرأيت } هي التي بمعنى أخبرني ،   فتتعدى لاثنين ،   أحدهما الذي ،   والآخر محذوف ،   فقدره الحوفي : أليس مستحقاً عذاب الله

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī estimates the omitted second object of arayta as “who is he?”
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r7.anchor: وقدره الزمخشري : من هو ،   ويدل على أنها بمعنى أخبرني

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r8.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads araytaka with the addressee kāf, since that kāf does not attach to visual perception.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r8.anchor: قراءة عبد الله أرأيتك بكاف الخطاب ،   لأن كاف الخطاب لا تلحق البصرية

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r9.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r9.claim: Al-Ḥawfī allows arayta to mean seeing with the eyes, requiring no ellipsis; the interrogative invites the listener to recall someone known by this trait.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r9.anchor: قال الحوفي : ويجوز أن تكون من رؤية البصر ،   فلا يكون في الكلام حذف ،   وهمزة الاستفهام تدل على التقرير والتفهيم ليتذكر السامع

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r10.claim: Al-dīn here means requital through reward and punishment.

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī paraphrases the question as asking whether one knows the person who denies requital.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r11.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : والمعنى هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-dīn as God’s law.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : { بالدين } : بحكم الله

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r13.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r13.claim: Mujāhid glosses al-dīn as the reckoning.
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r13.anchor: وقال مجاهد : بالحساب ،   وقيل : بالجزاء ،   وقيل : بالقرآن

ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:1/r14.claim: Other glosses take al-dīn as requital or as the Qurʾān.

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī proposes coordinating fa-dhālika with alladhī yukadhdhib, deleting arayta’s second object and using the following woe as its indication.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : بعد أن قدم فيما نقلناه من كلامه ما يدل على أن { فذلك الذي يدع } في موضع رفع ،   قال : وطريقة أخرى

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī’s accusative coordination is an unusual construction; the immediate, more eloquent parse makes fa-dhālika a nominative subject.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r8.anchor: فجعل فذلك في موضع نصب عطفاً على المفعول ،   وهو تركيب غريب

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r9.claim: The proposed coordination of one entity with another is invalid: fa-dhālika points to the same individual as alladhī yukadhdhib.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r9.anchor: لأن فذلك إشارة إلى الذي يكذب ،   فليسا بذاتين

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r10.claim: What al-Zamakhsharī calls an omitted answer to arayta is not an answer; it occupies the place of arayta’s second object.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r10.anchor: بل هو في موضع المفعول الثاني لأرأيت

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r11.claim: The interrogative hamza cannot enter نعم or بئس, which are performative expressions rather than statements.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r11.anchor: فهمزة الاستفهام لا نعلم دخولها على نعم ولا بئس ،   لأنهما إنشاء

ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r12.claim: Treating plural al-muṣallīn as a substitute for the singular alladhī by construing it generically is forced; the Qurʾān should follow the apparent syntax.
ABUHAYYAN:107:2/r12.anchor: لأن ضمير الذي يكذب معناه الجمع ،   فتكلف واضح ولا ينبغي أن يحمل القرآن إلا على ما اقتضاه ظاهر التركيب

ALUSI:107:1/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:1/r1.claim: The sūra is also called Sūrat Araʾayta, al-Dīn, and al-Takdhīb; most call it Meccan, while Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk are also cited for Medina, and Hibat Allāh divides its revelation between both cities.
ALUSI:107:1/r1.anchor: وتسمى سورة أرأيت والدين والتكذيب وهي مكية في قول الجمهور

ALUSI:107:1/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:1/r2.claim: The verse count is seven in the Iraqi tradition and six in other traditions.
ALUSI:107:1/r2.anchor: وآيها سبع في العراقي وست في الباقية

ALUSI:107:1/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:1/r3.claim: The question stimulates listeners to identify the denier, whom religious people must avoid and whose conduct they should shun; it also expresses astonishment.
ALUSI:107:1/r3.anchor: استفهام أريد بن تشويق السامع إلى تعرف المكذب وإن ذلك مما يجب على المتدين ليحترز عنه

ALUSI:107:1/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:1/r4.claim: The address may be to the Prophet or anyone suitable; raʾayta can mean know, taking one object, or figuratively inform me, taking two with an omitted second object.
ALUSI:107:1/r4.anchor: والخطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أو لكل من يصلح له والرؤية بمعنى المعرفة المتعدية لواحد

ALUSI:107:1/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r5.speaker: الحوفي
ALUSI:107:1/r5.claim: Al-Ḥawfī allows visual perception as the meaning of raʾayta; on either reading it can figuratively mean tell me, with the second object omitted.
ALUSI:107:1/r5.anchor: وقال الحوفي يجوز أن تكون بصرية وعلى الوجهين يجوز أن يتجوز بذلك عن الاخبار

ALUSI:107:1/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r6.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI:107:1/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads araʾaytaka with an added emphatic address-kāf after the tāʾ.
ALUSI:107:1/r6.anchor: قراءة عبد الله أرأيتك بكاف الخطاب المزيدة لتأكيد التاء

ALUSI:107:1/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:1/r7.claim: Al-dīn means recompense, as in the saying that one is repaid as one acts.
ALUSI:107:1/r7.anchor: والدين الجزاء وهو أحد معانيه ومنه كما تدين تدان

ALUSI:107:1/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:1/r9.claim: Others take al-dīn as Islam, or as the Qur'an or God's law; the latter interpretation is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās.
ALUSI:107:1/r9.anchor: أو الإسلام كما هو الأشهر ولعله مراد من فسره بالقرآن وكذا من فسره كابن عباس بحكم الله

ALUSI:107:1/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r10.speaker: الكسائي
ALUSI:107:1/r10.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads araʾayta without the hamza, by analogy with its present-tense form; the interrogative hamza helps explain the deletion.
ALUSI:107:1/r10.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي أرأيت بحذف الهمزة كأنه حمل الماضي في حذف همزته على مضارعه

ALUSI:107:1/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:1/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:1/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds al-Kisāʾī's reading better explained than deletion in the cited poetic line; attaching the interrogative hamza to past arā is another, weaker explanation.
ALUSI:107:1/r11.anchor: ومن هنا كانت هذه القراءة أقوى توجيهاً

ALUSI:107:7/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r12.claim: The sūra intensifies warning against these widespread vices as signs of denying religion; believers should flee them, since denial of religion lies behind every sin.
ALUSI:107:7/r12.anchor: والغرض التغليظ في أمر هذه الرذائل التي ابتلي بها كثير من الناس

ALUSI:107:7/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI:107:7/r17.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the sūra's main concern is denial of religion, using orphan-abuse as its identifying sign and the later vices to press the question whether such conduct is good or evil, like the rebuke in 5:91.
ALUSI:107:7/r17.anchor: فكأنه قيل أخبرني ما تقول فيمن يكذبون بالدين وفيمن يؤذون اليتيم

ALUSI:107:7/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:107:7/r23.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:107:7/r23.claim: A further analysis coordinates two entities and asks whether the deniers and orphan-pushers are in a good or bad state; al-Kashf objects that the pronoun cannot naturally refer to both groups and be replaced by worshippers.
ALUSI:107:7/r23.anchor: وجوز أيضاً أن يكون العطف عطف ذات على ذات فالاستخبار عن حال المكذبين وحال الداعين

BAGHAWI:107:1/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:1/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:107:1/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Māʿūn is Meccan and has seven verses.

BAGHAWI:107:1/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:1/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI:107:1/r2.claim: Muqatil says the sūra was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī.
BAGHAWI:107:1/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل : نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي

BAGHAWI:107:1/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:1/r3.speaker: السدي، مقاتل بن حيان، ابن كيسان
BAGHAWI:107:1/r3.claim: Al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Ibn Kaysan say it was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
BAGHAWI:107:1/r3.anchor: وقال السدي ، ومقاتل بن حيان ، وابن كيسان : في الوليد بن المغيرة

BAGHAWI:107:1/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:1/r4.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI:107:1/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says it was revealed about ʿAmr ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Makhzumi.
BAGHAWI:107:1/r4.anchor: قال الضحاك : نزلت في عمرو بن عائذ المخزومي

BAGHAWI:107:1/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:1/r5.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:107:1/r5.claim: ʿAta, transmitting from Ibn Abbas, says it concerns an unnamed hypocrite.
BAGHAWI:107:1/r5.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس : في رجل من المنافقين

BAGHAWI:107:1/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:107:1/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:107:1/r6.claim: The denied dīn means recompense and reckoning.
BAGHAWI:107:1/r6.anchor: ومعنى { يكذب بالدين } أي بالجزاء والحساب

BAYDAWI:107:1/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:1/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:1/r1.claim: The sūra’s Meccan or Medinan classification is disputed; it has seven verses.
BAYDAWI:107:1/r1.anchor: سورة الماعون مختلف فيها ، وآيها سبع آيات

BAYDAWI:107:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:1/r2.claim: Arāʾayta is an interrogative used to express amazement.

BAYDAWI:107:1/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:1/r3.speaker: قرئ
BAYDAWI:107:1/r3.claim: It is read arayta without hamza, assimilated to the imperfect; the interrogative opening may ease that form, and another reading adds kāf.
BAYDAWI:107:1/r3.anchor: وقرئ ( أريت ) بلا همزة إلحاقا بالمضارع ، ولعل تصديرها بحرف الاستفهام سهل أمرها ، و( أرأيتك ) بزيادة الكاف

BAYDAWI:107:1/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:1/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:1/r4.claim: Al-dīn may mean recompense or Islam.
BAYDAWI:107:1/r4.anchor: الذي يكذب بالدين بالجزاء أو الإسلام

BAYDAWI:107:1/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:107:1/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:107:1/r5.claim: Alladhī may be generic or refer to a known individual; the following verse supports the definite, known-person reading.
BAYDAWI:107:1/r5.anchor: و( الذي ) يحتمل الجنس والعهد ، ويؤيد الثاني قوله{ فذلك الذي يدع اليتيم }

BIQAI:107:1/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:1/r1.claim: The close of Quraysh commands gratitude through worship of God alone; this sūra explains that gratitude requires belief in recompense, which motivates noble conduct.
BIQAI:107:1/r1.anchor: وأمرهم آخر قريش بشكر نعمته بإفراده بالعبادة ، عرفهم أول هذه أن ذلك لا يتهيأ إلا بالتصديق بالجزاء الحامل على معالي الأخلاق

BIQAI:107:1/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:1/r2.claim: The sūra marvels at denial despite the evidence of divine wisdom and depicts the denier through repellent traits to induce belief and deter denial.
BIQAI:107:1/r2.anchor: وعجب ممن يكذب بالجزاء مع وضوح الدلالة عليه بحكمة الحكيم ، ووصف المكذب به بأوصاف هم منها في غاية النفرة

BIQAI:107:1/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:1/r3.claim: The address is directed specifically to Muhammad, the community's leader, since he alone fully understands this matter.
BIQAI:107:1/r3.anchor: فقال خاصاً بالخطاب رأس الأمة إشارة إلى أنه لا يفهم هذا الأمر حق فهمه غيره

BIQAI:107:1/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:1/r4.claim: Arāʾayta means “tell me,” addressed to the most perfect of creatures.

BIQAI:107:1/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:1/r5.claim: The denier actively rejects whoever tells him about the matter, whoever that speaker may be.
BIQAI:107:1/r5.anchor: أي يوقع التكذيب لمن يخبره كائناً من كان

BIQAI:107:1/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:1/r6.claim: Al-dīn here is recompense on Resurrection Day, the culmination of wisdom and of the law that commands noble morals and forbids their opposites.
BIQAI:107:1/r6.anchor: أي الجزائي الذي يكون يوم البعث الذي هو محط الحكمة

BIQAI:107:1/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:1/r7.claim: Denying either final recompense or the prescriptive religion entails denying the other.

BIQAI:107:1/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:107:1/r8.claim: Since arāʾayta means “tell me” and takes two objects, the omitted second object is understood as asking whether the denier deserves punishment.
BIQAI:107:1/r8.anchor: ولما كان فعل الرؤية بمعنى أخبرني ، المتعدي إلى مفعولين ، كان تقدير المفعول الثاني : أليس جديراً بالانتقام منه

BIQAI:107:1/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r9.speaker: الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:107:1/r9.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the warnings in 100:6, 103:2, and 102:3 to this sūra's account of conduct produced by ignorance, injustice, and attachment to wealth.
BIQAI:107:1/r9.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : لما تضمنت السور المتقدمة من الوعيد لمن انطوى على ما ذكر فيها

BIQAI:107:1/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r10.speaker: الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:107:1/r10.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says pushing or neglecting orphans, failing to urge feeding the poor, neglecting prayer, showing off, and withholding help can mark people professing Islam; the sūra identifies these as traits of those who deny judgment.
BIQAI:107:1/r10.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : لما تضمنت السور المتقدمة من الوعيد لمن انطوى على ما ذكر فيها

BIQAI:107:1/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:107:1/r11.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr cites the Prophetic saying that four combined traits make someone a complete hypocrite; no grading is stated.
BIQAI:107:1/r11.anchor: ومن هذا القبيل قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : " أربع من كن فيه كان منافقاً خالصاً "

BIQAI:107:1/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI:107:1/r12.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr also cites the saying that a fornicator is not a believer while fornicating; no grading is stated.
BIQAI:107:1/r12.anchor: وقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : " لا يزني الزاني حين يزني وهو مؤمن "

BIQAI:107:1/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:107:1/r13.speaker: الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير
BIQAI:107:1/r13.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says belief in recompense makes people avoid these traits, while deniers do not care about them; he warns believers not to imitate them and links their vices to earlier sūras.
BIQAI:107:1/r13.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر ابن الزبير : لما تضمنت السور المتقدمة من الوعيد لمن انطوى على ما ذكر فيها

DURR:107:1/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:107:1/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وعبد الله بن الزبير
DURR:107:1/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Zubayr report that Sūrat al-Māʿūn was revealed in Mecca.
DURR:107:1/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : أنزلت { أرأيت الذي يكذب } بمكة . وأخرج ابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن الزبير مثله .

DURR:107:1/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:107:1/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR:107:1/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the one who denies the dīn as a disbeliever.
DURR:107:1/r2.anchor: عن الحسن { أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين } قال : الكافر .

DURR:107:1/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:107:1/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR:107:1/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses al-dīn here as the reckoning.
DURR:107:1/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج { أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين } قال : بالحساب .

IBNATIYYA:107:1/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the sura is Meccan, as far as he knows without disagreement.

IBNATIYYA:107:1/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r2.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r2.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi says the sura is Medinan.

IBNATIYYA:107:1/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r3.claim: The opening question alerts the hearer to recall anyone he knows with the trait of denying requital.
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r3.anchor: هذا توقيف وتنبيه لتتذكر نفس السامع كل من يعرفه بهذه الصفة

IBNATIYYA:107:1/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r4.claim: Abu Amr sometimes pronounces the hamza in arayta.

IBNATIYYA:107:1/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r5.speaker: نافع وغيره
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r5.claim: Nafi and others do not pronounce the hamza in arayta.

IBNATIYYA:107:1/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r6.claim: Al-din means recompense, reward or punishment; here it is close to accounting.
IBNATIYYA:107:1/r6.anchor: و { الدين } الجزاء ثواباً وعقاباً ، والحساب هنا قريب من الجزاء

IBNKATHIR:107:1/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:1/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:107:1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies Surat al-Maʿun as Meccan.
IBNKATHIR:107:1/r1.anchor: تفسير السورة التي يذكر فيها الماعون وهي مكية

IBNKATHIR:107:1/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:107:1/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:107:1/r2.claim: Al-din here means resurrection, reckoning, and recompense.
IBNKATHIR:107:1/r2.anchor: يكذب بالدين ؟ وهو : المعاد والجزاء والثواب

KASHSHAF:107:1/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:1/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:1/r1.claim: The sūra is Meccan, though it is also said to be Medinan; it has seven verses.

KASHSHAF:107:1/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:1/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:1/r2.claim: The reading arayta deletes the hamza; it is not preferred because deletion belongs to the imperfect and Arabic usage does not attest rīt, though initial interrogation makes it easier; a cited line supplies rayta.

KASHSHAF:107:1/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:1/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF:107:1/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read arāytaka, adding the second-person suffix, as in the address in Sūrat al-Isrāʾ.
KASHSHAF:107:1/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : «أرأيتك » بزيادة حرف الخطاب

KASHSHAF:107:1/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:1/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:1/r4.claim: The question means: do you know who the denier of recompense is, if you do not already know?
KASHSHAF:107:1/r4.anchor: والمعنى : هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء

KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.claim: The preceding warning powerfully shows that sin signals weak faith and loose certainty; the text then adds a warning of woe for those who pray.
KASHSHAF:107:4/r1.anchor: وما أبلغه في التحذير من المعصية ،   وأنها جديرة بأن يستدل بها

KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.claim: Another syntax coordinates fa-dhālika with the denier, as a noun or description; the answer to “Have you seen?” is omitted and indicated by what follows, and the plural denotes the generic singular.
KASHSHAF:107:5/r5.anchor: وطريقة أخرى : أن يكون { فَذَلِكَ } عطفاً على { الذي يُكَذّبُ }

KASHSHAF:107:7/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:107:7/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:107:7/r5.claim: A report from the Prophet promises forgiveness to whoever recites Sūrat Araʾayta, provided that person pays zakāh.
KASHSHAF:107:7/r5.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم :  "  من قرأ ( سورة أرأيت )

MAWARDI:107:1/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:1/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:107:1/r1.claim: The sura is Meccan according to ʿAta and Jabir, but Medinan according to Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatada.
MAWARDI:107:1/r1.anchor: سورة الماعون مكية في قول عطاء وجابر . ومدنية في قول ابن عباس وقتادة .

MAWARDI:107:1/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:1/r2.speaker: عكرمة ومجاهد
MAWARDI:107:1/r2.claim: ʿIkrima and Mujahid take al-din here to mean the reckoning.
MAWARDI:107:1/r2.anchor: أحدها : يعني بالحساب ، قاله عكرمة ومجاهد .

MAWARDI:107:1/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:1/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:107:1/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas takes al-din to mean God's judgment.
MAWARDI:107:1/r3.anchor: الثاني : بحكم الله تعالى ، قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI:107:1/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:1/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:107:1/r4.claim: A third interpretation is requital, reward, and punishment.

MAWARDI:107:1/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:1/r5.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
MAWARDI:107:1/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say the sura was revealed about al-ʿAs b. Waʾil al-Sahmi.
MAWARDI:107:1/r5.anchor: أحدها : أنها نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي ، قاله الكلبي ومقاتل .

MAWARDI:107:1/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:1/r6.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:107:1/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says it was revealed about al-Walid b. al-Mughira.
MAWARDI:107:1/r6.anchor: الثاني : في الوليد بن المغيرة ، قاله السدي .

MAWARDI:107:1/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:1/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI:107:1/r7.claim: One reported view says it was revealed about Abu Jahl.

MAWARDI:107:1/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:1/r8.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI:107:1/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says it was revealed about ʿAmr b. ʿAʾidh.
MAWARDI:107:1/r8.anchor: الرابع : في عمرو بن عائذ ، قاله الضحاك .

MAWARDI:107:1/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:107:1/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI:107:1/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it concerned Abu Sufyan, who slaughtered a camel; when an orphan asked him for some, he struck the child with a stick.
MAWARDI:107:1/r9.anchor: الخامس : في أبي سفيان وقد نحر جزوراً ، فأتاه يتيم ، فسأله منها ، فقرعه بعصا ، قاله ابن جريج .

NASAFI:107:1/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:1/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:1/r1.claim: Sūrat al-Māʿūn is disputed as Meccan or Medinan and has seven verses.

NASAFI:107:1/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:107:1/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:107:1/r2.claim: The question asks whether you know who denies the recompense, as if to identify him for one who does not know.
NASAFI:107:1/r2.anchor: أي هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء من هو إن لم تعرفه

QURTUBI:107:1/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r1.speaker: عطاء وجابر وابن عباس
QURTUBI:107:1/r1.claim: The sūra has seven verses; ʿAṭāʾ, Jābir, and one report from Ibn ʿAbbās call it Meccan, while another report from Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and others call it Medinan.
QURTUBI:107:1/r1.anchor: وهي مكية ،   في قول عطاء وجابر وأحد قولي ابن عباس .   ومدنية ،   في قول له آخر

QURTUBI:107:1/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:1/r2.claim: Al-dīn means requital and accounting in the Hereafter, as discussed in al-Fātiḥa.
QURTUBI:107:1/r2.anchor: أي بالجزاء والحساب في الآخرة ،   وقد تقدم في " الفاتحة "

QURTUBI:107:1/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r3.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI:107:1/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the retained second hamza: the verb does not occur as rayta, and the interrogative alif eases the hamza to an alif.

QURTUBI:107:1/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:107:1/r4.claim: The speech has an omitted clause: “Have you seen the one who denies the Judgment—is he right or mistaken?”
QURTUBI:107:1/r4.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف ،   والمعنى : أرأيت الذي يكذب بالدين : أمصيب هو أم مخطئ

QURTUBI:107:1/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:107:1/r5.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that it was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil; al-Kalbī and Muqātil give the same identification.
QURTUBI:107:1/r5.anchor: فذكر أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال : نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي ،   وقاله الكلبي ومقاتل

QURTUBI:107:1/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r6.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI:107:1/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that it was revealed about an unnamed hypocrite.
QURTUBI:107:1/r6.anchor: وروى الضحاك عنه قال : نزلت في رجل من المنافقين

QURTUBI:107:1/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r7.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI:107:1/r7.claim: Al-Suddī says it was revealed about al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra.
QURTUBI:107:1/r7.anchor: وقال السدي : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

QURTUBI:107:1/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:107:1/r8.claim: Another view identifies the person as Abū Jahl.

QURTUBI:107:1/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r9.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI:107:1/r9.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also identifies the person as ʿAmr b. ʿĀʾidh.

QURTUBI:107:1/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:107:1/r10.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI:107:1/r10.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it was revealed about Abū Sufyān, who slaughtered a camel weekly and struck away an orphan who asked him for something.
QURTUBI:107:1/r10.anchor: قال ابن جريج : نزلت في أبي سفيان ،   وكان ينحر في كل أسبوع جزورا

RAZI:107:1/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r1.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:107:1/r1.claim: Some read arayta with the hamza omitted. Al-Zajjāj disfavours it because Arabs do not say rīt for raʾayt, though an initial interrogative can ease hamza deletion; the cited verse witnesses the form.
RAZI:107:1/r1.anchor: قرأ بعضهم { أريت } بحذف الهمزة ، قال الزجاج : وهذا ليس بالاختيار

RAZI:107:1/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:107:1/r2.claim: The poetic line “ṣāḥ hal rayta” is cited as evidence for the expression’s usage.
RAZI:107:1/r2.anchor: صاح هل ريت أو سمعت براع *** رد في الضرع ما قرى في العلاب

RAZI:107:1/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI:107:1/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd read araytaka with an added second-person marker, like the wording in 17:62.
RAZI:107:1/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ( أرأيتك ) بزيادة حرف الخطاب

RAZI:107:1/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:107:1/r4.claim: Arayta asks whether one has recognized who denies recompense; if not, the following verse identifies him as the person who pushes the orphan.
RAZI:107:1/r4.anchor: معناه هل عرفت الذي يكذب بالجزاء من هو ، فإن لم تعرفه : ( فهو الذي يدع اليتيم )

RAZI:107:1/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:107:1/r5.claim: Although phrased as a question, arayta intensifies astonishment, like asking what someone did and why he exposed himself to it.
RAZI:107:1/r5.anchor: هذا اللفظ وإن كان في صورة الاستفهام ، لكن الغرض بمثله المبالغة في التعجب

RAZI:107:1/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:107:1/r6.claim: One view takes the address as directed to the Prophet.
RAZI:107:1/r6.anchor: قيل : إنه خطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI:107:1/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:107:1/r7.claim: Another view makes it an address to every rational person: after clear proofs, how could someone risk everlasting punishment without purpose or trade the enduring great for fleeting worldly gain?
RAZI:107:1/r7.anchor: وقيل : بل خطاب لكل عاقل أي أرأيت يا عاقل هذا الذي يكذب بالدين

RAZI:107:1/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
RAZI:107:1/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the verse was revealed about Abū Sufyān, who slaughtered two camels weekly and struck an orphan with his stick when the child asked for meat.
RAZI:107:1/r8.anchor: فقال ابن جريج : نزلت في أبي سفيان كان ينحر جزورين في كل أسبوع

RAZI:107:1/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r9.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:107:1/r9.claim: Muqātil says it was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī, whose traits joined denial of Judgment Day with vile conduct.
RAZI:107:1/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل : نزلت في العاص بن وائل السهمي ، وكان من صفته الجمع

RAZI:107:1/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r10.speaker: السدي
RAZI:107:1/r10.claim: Al-Suddī identifies al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra as the person about whom the verse was revealed.
RAZI:107:1/r10.anchor: وقال السدي : نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

RAZI:107:1/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r11.speaker: الماوردي
RAZI:107:1/r11.claim: Al-Māwardī transmits that it concerned Abū Jahl, guardian of a naked orphan who asked for his own money and was pushed away; Quraysh mockingly sent him to seek Muhammad’s intercession, and Abū Jahl gave the money only because he feared the Prophet’s spears.
RAZI:107:1/r11.anchor: وحكى الماوردي أنها نزلت في أبي جهل ، وروي أنه كان وصيا ليتيم

RAZI:107:1/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:107:1/r12.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed about a hypocrite combining miserliness and ostentation.
RAZI:107:1/r12.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في منافق جمع بين البخل والمراءاة

RAZI:107:1/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r13.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI:107:1/r13.claim: Most commentators understand al-dīn here as reckoning and recompense; al-Rāzī favors this because someone denying Islam might still do good if convinced of resurrection, whereas unrestrained vice indicates denial of resurrection.
RAZI:107:1/r13.anchor: وهو قول أكثر المفسرين . أن المراد أرأيت الذي يكذب بالحساب والجزاء

RAZI:107:1/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:107:1/r14.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers “reckoning and recompense”: denial of resurrection explains persistent wrongdoing better than denial of Islam alone.
RAZI:107:1/r14.anchor: وحمله على هذا الوجه أولى لأن من ينكر الإسلام قد يأتي بالأفعال الحميدة

RAZI:107:1/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:107:1/r15.claim: One interpretation takes al-dīn as religion and Islam, including denial of God, prophethood, resurrection, or any law; unqualified “religion” in Islamic and Qurʾānic usage means Islam, while other religions require qualification.
RAZI:107:1/r15.anchor: أن يكون المراد من يكذب بنفس الدين والإسلام إما لأنه كان منكرا للصانع

RAZI:107:1/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r16.speaker: author
RAZI:107:1/r16.claim: A second explanation says false doctrines are not truly religion, since religion means submission to God, while such doctrines submit to appetite or conjecture.
RAZI:107:1/r16.anchor: هذه المقالات الباطلة ليست بدين ، لأن الدين هو الخضوع لله

RAZI:107:1/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:107:1/r17.speaker: author
RAZI:107:1/r17.claim: A general reading applies to anyone who denies the Resurrection: without hope of reward or fear of punishment, people would pursue desires and leave prohibitions unchecked, making denial of the afterlife a root of unbelief and sins.
RAZI:107:1/r17.anchor: أن إقدام الإنسان على الطاعات وإحجامه عن المحظورات إنما يكون للرغبة في الثواب
